Name: 17 Station Manual Anodize Line PL2211CN
Short description:
Manual anodizing line for type II or Type III with black dye.

Manufacture Date:  2022

This newer manual anodizing line was built in 2022 and has beeen used lightly since.

The line has a single truss mounted hoist suspended over the process that has Type II or Type III anodize with black dye or clear capability.

There are 17 stations on the line; the majority of the tanks are ¾” thick polypro while the seal and hot rinse tanks are stainless steel.

Station orientation and description are in the provided line layout. Tanks sit on a combination of fiberglass and poly I-beams.

Rectification for the anodize bath consists of a 200A 60V output American Plating Power Switchmode rectifier with ramp controls and digital programming cycles.

This line includes an air agitation blower, Tranter plate and frame heat exchanger, Thermal Care chiller, exhaust systems for the anodize and etch tanks, and filtration system for incoming water supply along with a 500 gallon purified water storage tank.

Line heating is via de-rated electric immersion heaters with tank mounted controls, overheat cutouts and tank low level switches.

This line is currently in use, owner will disconnect from facility, empty and power wash the equipment when it is sold but rigging and removal is up to buyer.

Name: 25 Station Automated Electroless Copper Plating Line PL2214CN
Short description: This electroless copper line was removed from an IBM facility in November of 2020. This line originally dates to 2000 but has been very well maintained through IBM’s PM program with several new tanks inserted in the last 5 years. The line is in excellent condition. This is a side arm hoist line which is low profile and was installed in a room with an 8’ ceiling. Process tanks on this line are heated by low pressure steam and grid type immersion coils (titanium and stainless). The line can be run manually without too much control retrofit. Allen Bradley hardware is used in this lines automation. This line has a stainless steel frame that sits atop the tanks and moves back and forth providing mechanical cathode agitation for every station. The frame is powered by a low rpm motor and linkage. Frame sits on rollers mounted to tank rim and goes back and forth slowly thus moving every flight bar in every tank back and forth. The side arm hoist and hoist structure come with the line. Multiple stainless steel flight bars also come with the line.
